theorem radialLevel_hasLaw (n : ℕ+) (h : ℕ) (i : Fin (h + 1))
    (x : Fin (h - i.val + 1) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n.val)) :
    let P := {p : Fin (2 ^ (64 * (h + 1)) + 1) // Even p.val ∧ 4 ≤ p.val}
    let B := Fin (h + 1) × P
    let C := fun b : B ↦
      ((Fin b.2.val.val × (Σ j : Fin (h - b.1.val + 1),
        Fin ((2 ^ (74 * (h + 1))) ^ j.val))) → Fin n.val)
    let degree := fun p : P ↦
      (⟨p.val.val, p.property.1, p.property.2, Nat.le_of_lt_succ p.val.isLt⟩ :
        {p : ℕ // Even p ∧ 4 ≤ p ∧ p ≤ 2 ^ (64 * (h + 1))})
    let S : ℕ := ∑ j : Fin (h - i.val + 1), (2 ^ (74 * (h + 1))) ^ j.val
    let a := fun p : P ↦ 1 / ((p.val.val : ℝ) ^ 4 * (S : ℝ) ^ 2 *
      Real.sqrt ((h - i.val + 1 : ℕ) * Real.log (2 * (2 : ℝ) ^ (64 * (h + 1)) * S)))
    let χ := fun r : ℝ ↦
      expNegInvGlue (r - 13 / 20) /
        (expNegInvGlue (r - 13 / 20) + expNegInvGlue (7 / 10 - r)) *
      (expNegInvGlue (1 - r) /
        (expNegInvGlue (1 - r) + expNegInvGlue (r - 19 / 20)))
    let c := ∏ j, χ (‖x j‖ / Real.sqrt n.val)
    let F := fun (u : Fin (h - i.val + 1) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n.val))
        (ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Σ b : B, C b)) ↦ ∑ p : P,
      angularDegreeComponent n h i (degree p) u
        (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun c : C (i, p) ↦ ξ ⟨(i, p), c⟩))
    let H := fun ξ ↦ if ∃ j, x j = 0 then 0
      else c * F (fun j ↦ NormedSpace.normalize (x j)) ξ
    HasLaw H (gaussianReal 0 (((n.val : ℝ) * c ^ 2 * ∑ p : P, (a p) ^ 2).toNNReal))
      (stdGaussian (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Σ b : B, C b)))

source.bounded_inventory: §4.1.1 Eqs. (13)–(16) and footnote 2; §4.2 linear-representation citation and one-point boundary of Lemma 4.4; §6.1 variance and fixed-location Gaussian passage leading into Eq. (51); §6.2 first use of Fact 10 as corroboration and downstream use.

TYPING: n : ℕ+ is the positive dimension; h : ℕ is the depth parameter; i : Fin (h+1) ranges over 0 through h.

x is a fixed deterministic trailing block vector, with Fin (h-i+1) indexing source blocks i through h. Every full location restricts to this vector and every such tail occurs. The coefficient vector is the variable of the measured function, not an extra theorem premise.
STANDING: Large n and the prescribed choice h(n) govern the hard-family application, not the isolated identity. The formula is valid for every positive n and natural h, including h=0 and i=h. This does not extend admissibility.
derived_not_assumed: Nonzero participating blocks give unit normalized directions; the zero branch is unconditional.
Coefficient measurability is of the finite sum of fixed linear evaluations, or the constant-zero function on the zero branch.
No c>0, cutoff support/range, beta_i, conditioning, admissibility, moment, or regularity binder is needed.

definition_audit.cutoff: Both quotient arguments use the paper's unscaled rho(t)=exp(-1/t) for t>0 and 0 otherwise. Breakpoints 13/20, 7/10, 19/20, and 1 are 0.65, 0.7, 0.95, and 1. The two arguments of each denominator sum to 1/20, so one is positive even at the breakpoints; the Lean division does not insert an unadvertised 0/0 convention. Transition rescaling would change the formula.
definition_audit.product: The local c multiplies exactly one chi(norm x_j / sqrt n) per participating block, not a cutoff of an aggregate norm or a gate product.
definition_audit.carrier: The finite degree subtype includes 4,6,…,2^(64(h+1)) including the upper endpoint; degree only transports the same numeric value to the angular component's subtype. For b=(l,p), an ordered position is (copy of the p-fold power, trailing block offset j, one of K^j positions in that block), K=2^(74(h+1)). All assignments of Fin n to these positions index n^(p S_l) tensor coordinates. The dependent sum over all (l,p) realizes the paper's full Euclidean orthogonal direct sum, not a symmetric-tensor quotient or a single marginal. The (i,p) projection uses exactly its own coordinates; toLp retypes the Euclidean vector without scaling.
definition_audit.angular_and_field: The Eq. (14) amplitude uses p^4, S_i^2, and sqrt((h-i+1) log(2 P S_i)), and Eq. (15) sums angular components (including their sqrt(n) factor) before forming the local H. On nonzero blocks, normalize is x_j divided by its Euclidean norm. The explicit zero test agrees with §4.2's extension and does not add an off-source branch.
definition_audit.variance: The right-hand parameter is the variance n*c^2*sum_p a_i,p^2, not its square root or a square of the sum. The product and summands are nonnegative, so toNNReal preserves the value. If a participating block vanishes, chi(0)=0 because the first numerator is rho(-13/20) and its denominator contains rho(7/10)>0; the product and H vanish. If all blocks are nonzero but c=0, H still vanishes. Both yield the same centered Dirac law, not a positive-variance density.
